penalty_min: 10 days or 32 hours community service (first); 30 days (second); 1 year with work release (third); 10 years hard labor (fourth+)
penalty_max: 6 months (first); 6 months (second); 5 years hard labor (third); 30 years hard labor (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle, aircraft, watercraft, or other means of conveyance
While under the influence of alcoholic beverages or any controlled dangerous substance
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 10 days or 32 hours community service (first); 30 days (second); 1 year with or without hard labor (third, minimum 6 months without probation or parole); 10 years hard labor (fourth+, minimum 10 years without probation or parole)
enhancements: Child under 12 in vehicle (additional penalties under § 14:98.4)
Fourth or subsequent (Felony — 10-30 years hard labor)
notes: Louisiana uses 'DWI' (Driving While Intoxicated). Implied consent under La. R.S. § 32:661. Refusal results in administrative license suspension. 10-year lookback period for enhancement. Ignition interlock required for all offenses. Louisiana has some of the harshest DWI penalties nationally for repeat offenders.

penalty_min: 10 days or 32 hours community service
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while intoxicated
BAC .08 or higher or impairment shown
No prior DWI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 10 days imprisonment or 32 hours community service; substance abuse evaluation; driver improvement program; 90-day license suspension
enhancements: BAC .20+ (minimum 48 hours imprisonment, mandatory ignition interlock 12 months)
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. License suspension 90 days (restricted license may be available with ignition interlock). Diversion programs available in some parishes.

penalty_min: 30 days (second); 1 year (third); 10 years (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while intoxicated
Defendant has prior DWI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 30 days (second); 1 year hard labor, minimum 6 months without suspension (third); 10 years hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension (fourth+)
notes: Fourth offense DWI is 10-30 years at hard labor — one of the harshest in the nation. Third offense requires minimum 6 months incarceration without suspension. Louisiana counts convictions within 10 years.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_min: Same as alcohol DWI
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any controlled dangerous substance as defined by the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI
notes: Louisiana does not have a per se drug DWI provision — prosecution must prove actual impairment. Includes prescription medications that impair driving.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle in a criminally negligent or reckless manner
notes: Misdemeanor with relatively low penalties. Common plea reduction from DWI. Louisiana uses 'reckless operation' rather than 'reckless driving.'

offense_class: Felony (death/serious bodily injury); Misdemeanor (non-serious injury or property damage)
penalty_max: 10 years hard labor (death/serious injury); 6 months (property/minor injury)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Resulting in death, injury, or property damage
Defendant intentionally failed to stop and give identifying information and render aid
enhancements: Death (imprisonment at hard labor not more than 10 years)
notes: Hit-and-run involving death or serious injury is a felony with hard labor. Must stop, give name, address, and license information, and render reasonable assistance.

penalty_min: 5 years hard labor (minimum 3 years without suspension)
elements: Defendant killed another human being while engaged in the operation of a motor vehicle
While intoxicated (BAC .08+ or under the influence of drugs)
Or while in violation of certain traffic laws
mandatory_minimum: Minimum 5 years, at least 3 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension of sentence
notes: Vehicular homicide in Louisiana carries 5-30 years at hard labor — among the harshest nationally. BAC level at time of offense significantly impacts mandatory minimum. Separate from negligent homicide.

elements: Defendant killed a human being
By criminal negligence
notes: Negligent homicide covers vehicular deaths caused by criminal negligence without intoxication. Less severe than vehicular homicide (DWI-related). Criminal negligence is a higher standard than civil negligence.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public highway
While driving privilege was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension
notes: Third offense driving while suspended is a felony in Louisiana. DWI-related suspensions carry additional consequences. Notice of suspension creates presumption of knowledge.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (on foot); Felony (aggravated flight — vehicle endangering human life)
penalty_max: 6 months (on foot); 5 years hard labor (aggravated flight, first); 10 years (aggravated flight, second+)
elements: Defendant intentionally refused to stop or fled from a law enforcement officer
After being given a visual or audible signal to stop
Aggravated: flight by vehicle that creates serious risk to human life
enhancements: Aggravated flight (vehicle, endangering life) — felony up to 5 years hard labor
Serious bodily injury to another person during flight
Second or subsequent aggravated flight (up to 10 years)
notes: Simple flight (on foot) is a misdemeanor. Aggravated flight from an officer (vehicle, endangering human life) is a felony. Louisiana specifies 'hard labor' for felony sentences.

statute_title: Possession of a Controlled Dangerous Substance (Schedule I)
offense_class: Felony (Schedule I/II); Misdemeanor (Schedule III-V for smaller amounts)
penalty_max: 5 years hard labor (Schedule I, first); 5 years hard labor (Schedule II, first); lesser for III-V
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled dangerous substance
Classified in Schedule I
enhancements: Second offense (up to 10 years hard labor)
Third or subsequent (up to 20 years hard labor)
notes: Louisiana reformed drug possession laws significantly in 2017 (Justice Reinvestment). Possession penalties were reduced. Schedule I/II possession is still a felony. Drug court diversion widely available.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (14g or less, first/second); Misdemeanor (14g-2.5 lbs, first); Felony (third+ or large amounts)
penalty_max: 15 days (14g or less, first); 6 months (14g or less, second); 5 years (14g-2.5 lbs, first); 20 years (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana
enhancements: Amount over 14 grams (felony for repeat offenders)
Third or subsequent (up to 20 years hard labor)
notes: Louisiana reformed marijuana penalties in 2021. Possession of 14 grams or less is a misdemeanor (max 15 days first offense). Larger amounts remain felonies for repeat offenders. Louisiana has a medical marijuana program.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
enhancements: Second offense (up to 10 years hard labor)
Third or subsequent (up to 20 years hard labor)
notes: Cocaine is Schedule II in Louisiana. First possession is up to 5 years hard labor after 2017 reform (previously up to 5 years without reform). Drug court diversion available.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
enhancements: Second offense (up to 10 years hard labor)
Third or subsequent (up to 20 years hard labor)
notes: Meth is Schedule II. Same penalties as cocaine possession. 2017 reform reduced maximums. Drug court available for eligible offenders.

statute_title: Distribution or Possession with Intent to Distribute — Large Amounts
penalty_min: 5 years hard labor (cocaine 28g+); 10 years hard labor (heroin 28g+)
penalty_max: 40 years hard labor (cocaine 28g-199g); 99 years hard labor (heroin 400g+); life (Schedule I large amounts)
elements: Defendant produced, manufactured, distributed, or dispensed, or possessed with intent to distribute
A controlled dangerous substance in trafficking amounts
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory minimum without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension for trafficking-level amounts
enhancements: Near school, church, or housing project (additional penalties under § 40:981.3)
notes: Louisiana has specific trafficking penalties with mandatory minimums based on weight. Cocaine 28g+, heroin 28g+, and meth 28g+ trigger enhanced trafficking provisions. Some of the harshest drug penalties in the nation.

statute_title: Distribution of a Controlled Dangerous Substance
penalty_min: 2 years hard labor (Schedule I, first)
penalty_max: 30 years hard labor (Schedule I, first); 60 years (Schedule I, second); life (Schedule I, third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally produced, manufactured, distributed, or dispensed
Or possessed with intent to produce, manufacture, distribute, or dispense
A controlled dangerous substance
mandatory_minimum: Minimum 2 years without benefit of probation or suspension (Schedule I, first)
enhancements: Second offense (Schedule I: 5-60 years hard labor)
Third or subsequent (Schedule I: life imprisonment at hard labor)
Near school or public housing (enhanced under § 40:981.3)
notes: Distribution of Schedule I substances carries severe penalties. Third offense carries mandatory life imprisonment. School zone enhancement adds consecutive time.

penalty_min: 5 years hard labor (meth manufacturing)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled dangerous substance
mandatory_minimum: Minimum 5 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension (meth manufacturing under § 40:967(A))
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a minor (enhanced)
notes: Manufacturing is covered under the distribution statutes. Meth manufacturing has specific enhanced provisions. Environmental contamination remediation costs may be assessed.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
Knowing or under circumstances where one reasonably should know that it will be used for controlled substance purposes
notes: Possession is a misdemeanor. Sale or delivery of paraphernalia is also a misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor is a felony.

penalty_min: 2 years hard labor (Schedule I, first)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled dangerous substance
With intent to produce, manufacture, distribute, or dispense
mandatory_minimum: Same as distribution
notes: Possession with intent to distribute carries the same penalties as actual distribution in Louisiana. Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, and other evidence.

penalty_min: Life imprisonment at hard labor without benefit of parole, probation, or suspension
elements: Defendant had specific intent to kill or inflict great bodily harm
And one or more aggravating circumstances exist (e.g., victim was police officer, killing during felony, killing for hire, victim under 12, serial killing)
mandatory_minimum: Life at hard labor without parole (if death penalty not imposed)
notes: Louisiana retains the death penalty for first-degree murder. If the death penalty is not sought or imposed, the sentence is mandatory life at hard labor without parole. Unanimous jury required for conviction.

penalty_min: Life imprisonment at hard labor without benefit of parole, probation, or suspension
penalty_max: Life imprisonment at hard labor without parole
elements: Defendant had specific intent to kill or inflict great bodily harm
Without the aggravating circumstances required for first-degree murder
Or defendant engaged in the perpetration of certain felonies during which a human being was killed
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory life imprisonment at hard labor without parole, probation, or suspension
notes: Second-degree murder carries mandatory life without parole — same sentence as first-degree without the death penalty. This is one of the most severe second-degree murder penalties nationally. Includes felony murder rule.

elements: Defendant killed a human being
When the offender has a specific intent to kill or inflict great bodily harm
While in sudden passion or heat of blood immediately caused by provocation sufficient to deprive an average person of self-control
notes: Louisiana manslaughter covers what other states call voluntary manslaughter. Up to 40 years at hard labor — very severe for manslaughter. 'Sudden passion' or 'heat of blood' is the mitigating factor.

elements: Defendant killed a human being by criminal negligence
enhancements: Negligent homicide with a motor vehicle while DWI — charged as vehicular homicide under § 14:32.1
notes: Louisiana uses 'negligent homicide' instead of 'involuntary manslaughter.' Criminal negligence is conduct that demonstrates gross deviation from the standard of care. Maximum 5 years hard labor.

penalty_max: 6 months (misdemeanor) or 5 years hard labor (with firearm under § 14:37.4)
elements: Defendant committed an assault
With a dangerous weapon
enhancements: With a firearm (Aggravated Assault with a Firearm — felony, up to 10 years hard labor under § 14:37.4)
notes: Louisiana defines aggravated assault as assault with a dangerous weapon. Aggravated assault with a firearm (§ 14:37.4) carries up to 10 years at hard labor. Distinction between assault (attempt) and battery (contact) is maintained.

elements: Defendant committed an assault on another person
An assault is an attempt to commit a battery or the intentional placing of another in reasonable apprehension of receiving a battery
notes: Simple assault in Louisiana is a threat-based offense — no physical contact required. Physical contact is 'battery.' Low penalties — 90 days max and $200 fine.

elements: Defendant committed a battery upon another person
A battery is the intentional use of force or violence upon the person of another
Or the administration of a poison or noxious liquid or substance to another
enhancements: Causing serious bodily injury — aggravated battery under § 14:34
notes: Simple battery is a misdemeanor. Louisiana maintains the assault (threat) / battery (contact) distinction. Aggravated battery (§ 14:34) causing serious bodily injury is up to 10 years hard labor.

elements: Defendant took anything of value belonging to another from the person of another or in the immediate control of another
By use of force or intimidation, but not armed with a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Armed with a dangerous weapon — Armed Robbery (§ 14:64)
notes: Simple robbery is the base robbery offense without a weapon. Up to 7 years at hard labor. Louisiana has several robbery classifications.

penalty_min: 10 years hard labor without benefit of parole, probation, or suspension
elements: Defendant took anything of value from the person or immediate control of another
By use of force or intimidation
While armed with a dangerous weapon
mandatory_minimum: 10 years without benefit of parole, probation, or suspension
enhancements: Use of a firearm (additional mandatory consecutive sentence under § 14:64.3)
notes: Armed robbery carries 10-99 years at hard labor — among the harshest in the nation. Minimum 10 years without parole. Armed robbery with a firearm under § 14:64.3 adds a mandatory 5 years consecutive.

penalty_min: Life at hard labor without parole (aggravated); 5 years (simple under § 14:45)
penalty_max: Death or life without parole (aggravated); 5 years (simple); 40 years (second degree under § 14:44.1)
elements: Defendant forcibly seized and carried another from one place to another
Aggravated: with intent to extort, use as hostage, physical injury, or sexual abuse
mandatory_minimum: Life at hard labor without parole (aggravated kidnapping if death penalty not imposed); 5 years without probation/parole (second degree, if victim under 18)
notes: Louisiana has aggravated kidnapping (capital offense), second-degree kidnapping (§ 14:44.1, up to 40 years), and simple kidnapping (§ 14:45, up to 5 years). Aggravated kidnapping carries death or mandatory life.

penalty_min: 6 years hard labor without probation/parole (aggravated)
penalty_max: 20 years hard labor (aggravated); 15 years hard labor (simple under § 14:52)
elements: Defendant intentionally set fire to or damaged by explosive a structure
Aggravated: when the structure is foreseeable to be occupied by one or more persons
mandatory_minimum: 6 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension (aggravated)
enhancements: Resulting in bodily harm or death
notes: Aggravated arson (occupied building) carries 6-20 years at hard labor with a 6-year mandatory minimum. Simple arson (unoccupied) is up to 15 years.

penalty_min: 10 years hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant had specific intent to commit first-degree murder
And committed an overt act toward the commission thereof
mandatory_minimum: 10 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Attempted first-degree murder carries 10-50 years at hard labor. Attempted second-degree murder carries 10-50 years. Both have mandatory minimums without parole.

penalty_min: 1 year hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant committed an assault upon another person
With a firearm
mandatory_minimum: 1 year without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Aggravated assault with a firearm is a specific statute with harsher penalties than general aggravated assault. 1-year mandatory minimum without parole.

penalty_max: 6 months (under $1,000); 5 years (with or without hard labor, $1,000-$4,999); 10 years (hard labor, $5,000-$24,999); 20 years (hard labor, $25,000+)
elements: Defendant misappropriated or took anything of value belonging to another
Either without the consent of the other to the misappropriation or taking
Or by means of fraudulent conduct, practices, or representations
With intent to deprive the other permanently of the thing of value
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (felony regardless of value)
notes: Louisiana unified theft statute. Felony threshold is $1,000. Multiple value tiers with increasing penalties. Theft of a firearm (§ 14:67.15) is always a felony.

penalty_max: 5 years ($1,000-$4,999); 10 years hard labor ($5,000-$24,999); 20 years hard labor ($25,000+)
elements: Defendant took or misappropriated property of another
With intent to permanently deprive
Value $1,000 or more
notes: Louisiana does not use 'grand theft' terminology. Felony theft based on $1,000 threshold with multiple tiers.

elements: Defendant took or misappropriated property of another
With intent to permanently deprive
Value under $1,000
notes: Misdemeanor theft for property under $1,000. Diversion available in some parishes for first offenders.

penalty_max: 6 months (under $500, first); 2 years hard labor (third+, under $1,000); felony penalties for $1,000+
fine_max: $500 (first, under $500); $2,000 (third+); felony fines for higher values
elements: Defendant committed theft of goods held for sale in a retail establishment
By concealing, taking, or otherwise appropriating goods
enhancements: Third or subsequent (up to 2 years hard labor even for misdemeanor amounts)
notes: Louisiana has a separate shoplifting statute. Third offense shoplifting carries up to 2 years at hard labor even for amounts under $1,000. Civil recovery also available to merchants.

penalty_min: 1 year hard labor (inhabited dwelling)
elements: Defendant entered a structure, vehicle, or watercraft
Without authorization
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
mandatory_minimum: 1 year without probation, parole, or suspension if of an inhabited dwelling
enhancements: Inhabited dwelling (mandatory minimum 1 year without probation/parole)
Aggravated Burglary — while armed or committing battery (§ 14:60)
notes: Simple burglary is up to 12 years hard labor. Aggravated burglary (§ 14:60 — entry while armed or committing battery) carries 1-30 years hard labor.

statute_title: Simple Burglary of an Inhabited Dwelling
penalty_min: 1 year hard labor without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant entered an inhabited dwelling without authorization
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
mandatory_minimum: 1 year without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
enhancements: While armed (Aggravated Burglary — 1-30 years hard labor)
notes: Burglary of an inhabited dwelling has a 1-year mandatory minimum without parole. 'Inhabited' means used as a place of abode whether or not occupied at the time.

statute_title: Unauthorized Use of a Motor Vehicle
elements: Defendant intentionally took or used a motor vehicle belonging to another
Without the owner's consent
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (up to 5 years hard labor)
notes: Louisiana's motor vehicle theft statute. Separate from general theft. Carjacking (§ 14:64.2) is a separate, much more serious offense (up to 20 years hard labor).

penalty_max: 6 months (under $1,000); 10 years hard labor ($1,000-$4,999); 20 years hard labor ($5,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally procured, received, or concealed stolen things
Knowing or having good reason to believe the things were stolen
With intent to deprive the owner permanently
notes: Louisiana uses 'illegal possession of stolen things.' Value tiers match the theft statute. The 'good reason to believe' standard is less than actual knowledge.

penalty_max: 6 months (under $1,000); 2 years hard labor ($1,000-$49,999); 3 years hard labor ($50,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged the property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Louisiana uses 'criminal damage to property.' Value tiers determine whether it's a misdemeanor or felony. Restitution typically ordered.

elements: Defendant entered upon immovable property of another without authorization
After having been forbidden to do so by the owner or authorized agent
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (up to 90 days)
notes: Louisiana criminal trespass requires notice (verbal, posted signs, or enclosure). Simple trespass is a misdemeanor. Trespass of critical infrastructure carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant intentionally damaged the property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Louisiana uses 'criminal damage to property' — same statute as vandalism entry.

penalty_min: 30 days (second offense, minimum without suspension)
penalty_max: 6 months (first); 1 year (second); 3 years hard labor (child or pregnant victim); 5 years hard labor (strangulation or aggravated under § 14:34.9)
elements: Defendant committed a battery upon a family member or household member as defined by the Protection from Domestic Abuse Act
Or dating partner
mandatory_minimum: Minimum 30 days (second offense, without probation or suspension); minimum 1 year (aggravated — strangulation, child, pregnant)
enhancements: Child present or pregnant victim (up to 3 years hard labor)
Strangulation (up to 3 years hard labor under § 14:35.3(L))
Aggravated domestic abuse battery — causing serious bodily injury (§ 14:34.9, up to 30 years)
notes: Louisiana has a specific domestic abuse battery statute with escalating penalties. Aggravated domestic abuse battery (§ 14:34.9 — serious injury) carries 1-30 years hard labor with a 1-year mandatory minimum. Mandatory arrest policy.

elements: Defendant intentionally used force or violence upon a family or household member
Or dating partner
notes: Same statute as domestic violence entry. Federal firearms prohibition applies upon conviction (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9)). Family or household member includes spouses, former spouses, co-parents, and cohabitants.

penalty_min: 1 year hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant intentionally or criminally negligently caused unjustifiable pain or suffering to a child
Or mistreated or neglected a child
mandatory_minimum: 1 year without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Louisiana's cruelty to juveniles statute covers abuse, neglect, and endangerment. 1-year mandatory minimum. DCFS investigation accompanies criminal charges.

penalty_min: 2 years hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant committed cruelty to a juvenile that results in serious bodily injury
Or the child required medical treatment for injuries
mandatory_minimum: 2 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Second-degree cruelty to juveniles (serious bodily injury) carries 2-40 years at hard labor with a 2-year mandatory minimum. First-degree (death) carries 10-40 years.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (subsequent or with additional crimes)
elements: A protective order was issued under the Domestic Abuse Assistance Act or Protection from Dating Violence Act
Defendant intentionally violated the order
mandatory_minimum: 14 days (first, if physical abuse involved); increased mandatory for subsequent
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation (felony, up to 2 years hard labor)
notes: Louisiana takes protective order violations seriously. First violation with abuse carries a mandatory 14-day jail sentence. Subsequent violations are felonies.

elements: Defendant willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly followed or harassed another person
Such that the victim felt seriously alarmed, annoyed, or harassed
And the conduct would cause a reasonable person to feel seriously alarmed, annoyed, or harassed
enhancements: Second or subsequent (felony, up to 5 years hard labor)
notes: Stalking requires repeated conduct. First offense is a misdemeanor. Second offense becomes a felony. Cyberstalking is a separate offense under § 14:40.3.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Felony (if against minor or second+)
elements: Defendant, using electronic communication, transmitted threats, harassment, or repeated unwanted messages
With intent to harass, intimidate, or cause emotional distress
notes: Louisiana has specific cyberstalking/online harassment statutes. General harassment may also be charged as disturbing the peace under § 14:103.

statute_title: Abuse of the Infirm — Cruelty to Persons with Infirmities
penalty_min: 1 year hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant intentionally or criminally negligently mistreated, neglected, or abused a person with an infirmity (including elderly)
By an act that caused unjustifiable physical or mental suffering
mandatory_minimum: 1 year without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Louisiana has a specific statute for cruelty to persons with infirmities, which covers elder abuse. 1-year mandatory minimum. Financial exploitation of the infirm (§ 14:93.4) carries up to 15 years.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (general); Felony (concealed by prohibited person under § 14:95.1)
penalty_max: 6 months (general); 5 years hard labor (convicted felon under § 14:95.1)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
Or carried a firearm while intoxicated or on certain prohibited premises
notes: Louisiana enacted permitless concealed carry effective July 4, 2024. Illegal carrying now primarily applies to prohibited persons, those carrying while intoxicated, and carrying in restricted locations.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
penalty_min: 5 years hard labor without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm or carried a concealed weapon
Defendant has been convicted of certain enumerated felonies
mandatory_minimum: 5 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension (first); 10 years (second+)
enhancements: Second or subsequent (minimum 10 years without probation/parole)
notes: Louisiana has one of the harshest felon-in-possession statutes. 5-year mandatory minimum without parole for first offense. 10-year mandatory for second. Applies to conviction of enumerated felonies, not all felonies.

statute_title: Illegal Carrying of Weapons — Prohibited Person
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
While a prohibited person or in a prohibited location or condition (intoxicated)
notes: With 2024 permitless carry, this applies to prohibited persons (felons, domestic abusers, those under 18), those carrying while intoxicated, and restricted locations (courthouses, schools, etc.).

statute_title: Illegal Use of Weapons or Dangerous Instrumentalities
offense_class: Felony (if injury or at occupied structure); Misdemeanor (general)
penalty_max: 2 years hard labor (general); 5 years hard labor (at inhabited dwelling); 10 years (injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally discharged a firearm
Where it was foreseeable that it might result in death or great bodily harm to a human being
enhancements: At an inhabited dwelling (up to 5 years hard labor)
Resulting in injury (up to 10 years hard labor)
notes: Covers reckless discharge, shooting into occupied structures, and other dangerous use of weapons. Shooting into an inhabited dwelling is a serious felony.

elements: Defendant intentionally used, possessed, transferred, or attempted to transfer the personal identifying information of another
To obtain, possess, or transfer anything of value
Without the authorization or consent of the other person
notes: Identity theft is a felony in Louisiana carrying up to 10 years at hard labor. Covers SSN, driver's license, bank account, and other identifying information.

elements: Defendant misappropriated anything of value entrusted to the defendant
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Embezzlement is charged as misappropriation under the unified theft statute. Same value tiers apply. Common in employee and fiduciary situations.

elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud, made or altered a writing or object
So that it purports to be the act of another
Or to have been executed at a time, place, or in a manner different than was in fact the case
notes: Forgery is a felony carrying up to 10 years at hard labor. Covers documents, checks, deeds, and any writing. Uttering (presenting a forged document) is included.

statute_title: Counterfeiting — Forgery of Currency or Government Documents
elements: Defendant made, altered, or possessed counterfeit currency or government documents
With intent to defraud
notes: Charged under the forgery statute. Primarily a federal offense. State charges may apply for possession of counterfeit bills.

elements: Defendant issued a check or draft knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
And the check was dishonored upon presentation
notes: Louisiana has a separate worthless checks statute. Intent to defraud may be inferred from failure to make good within 10 days of notice.

penalty_max: 5 years hard labor (under $1,000); 10 years hard labor ($1,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or misleading material statement in support of an insurance claim
With intent to defraud
notes: Louisiana has specific insurance fraud statutes. Covers auto, health, property, and life insurance fraud. Restitution and civil penalties also apply.

elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud, used or attempted to use a credit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, revoked, or unauthorized
notes: Louisiana has a specific credit card fraud statute. May also be charged as identity theft or theft by deception.

fine_max: $500,000 or twice the amount involved, whichever is greater
elements: Defendant knowingly conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction involving proceeds of specified criminal activity
With intent to promote the carrying on of specified criminal activity or to conceal the nature/source/ownership of the proceeds
notes: Louisiana money laundering carries up to 20 years at hard labor and severe fines. Applies to proceeds from any specified criminal activity. Forfeiture provisions also apply.

statute_title: Theft by Fraud (Theft by Fraudulent Conduct)
elements: Defendant obtained anything of value by means of fraudulent conduct, practices, or representations
With intent to deprive the owner permanently
notes: General fraud is charged as theft by fraudulent conduct under Louisiana's unified theft statute. Covers false representations, con schemes, and fraudulent inducement.

elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in the touching of the anus or genitals of the victim
Using any instrumentality or any part of the body of the offender
Without the consent of the victim
The act was for the purpose of arousing or gratifying sexual desires
enhancements: Victim under 13 (enhanced — charged as aggravated sexual battery under § 14:43.5)
notes: Sexual battery is up to 10 years hard labor. Louisiana distinguishes sexual battery (touching) from rape (penetration). Sex offender registration required.

penalty_min: Life at hard labor without parole
penalty_max: Life at hard labor without parole (death penalty for child victims held unconstitutional by Kennedy v. Louisiana)
elements: Defendant committed an act of sexual intercourse without the victim's lawful consent
When the victim resists to the utmost but is overcome by force
Or is prevented from resisting by threats of great and immediate bodily harm
Or when the victim is under 13 regardless of consent
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment at hard labor without benefit of parole, probation, or suspension
notes: First-degree rape (aggravated rape) carries mandatory life without parole. Second-degree rape (§ 14:42.1) carries 5-40 years without parole. Third-degree rape (§ 14:43) carries up to 25 years hard labor. Sex offender registration is lifetime.

elements: Defendant intentionally exposed the genitals, pubic hair, anus, vulva, or female breast nipple
In a public place or place open to public view
With the intent of arousing sexual desire or simulating sexual activity
enhancements: Third or subsequent (felony, up to 3 years hard labor)
Exposure to a minor (enhanced — may trigger sex offender registration)
notes: First two offenses are misdemeanors. Third offense is a felony. Exposure to minors may trigger sex offender registration.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first/second); Felony (third+ or involving a minor)
penalty_max: 6 months (first); 6 months (second, mandatory 5 days); 5 years hard labor (third+); 20 years hard labor (involving minor)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse for compensation
Or solicited another for prostitution
mandatory_minimum: 5 days (second offense); 2 years without probation (third+)
enhancements: Third or subsequent (felony, 2-5 years hard labor without probation)
Involving a minor (15-50 years under human trafficking)
Patronizing a person who is a victim of human trafficking (felony)
notes: Louisiana treats both buyer and seller as criminal actors. Third offense prostitution is a felony. Human trafficking charges (§ 14:46.2) apply when minors are involved — extremely severe penalties.

penalty_min: 2 years hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension (possession); 5 years (production/distribution)
penalty_max: 10 years hard labor (possession); 20 years hard labor (production/distribution)
elements: Defendant possessed visual depictions of a child engaged in sexual conduct
Or produced, distributed, or sold such material
mandatory_minimum: 2 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension (possession); 5 years (production/distribution)
notes: Each image/video is a separate count. Mandatory minimum 2 years for possession. Production and distribution carry 5-year mandatory minimums. Sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
penalty_min: 2 years hard labor without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant is required to register under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Law
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update information
mandatory_minimum: 2 years without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Louisiana has a 2-year mandatory minimum for failure to register — among the harshest nationally. Must register within 3 business days. Lifetime registration for many offenses.

statute_title: Felony Carnal Knowledge of a Juvenile
penalty_max: 10 years hard labor (with or without hard labor)
elements: Defendant, who is 17 or older, had sexual intercourse with consent of a person who is 13 to 16 years old
When the age difference between the defendant and the victim is 4 or more years
enhancements: Victim under 13 (First Degree Rape — mandatory life without parole)
notes: Louisiana's age of consent is 17. Felony carnal knowledge covers consensual sex with 13-16 year olds when the age difference is 4+ years. Misdemeanor carnal knowledge (§ 14:80.1) covers situations with smaller age gaps. Under 13 is first-degree rape.

elements: Defendant engaged in an act in a violent or tumultuous manner
Such that it disturbed the public peace or decorum
notes: Louisiana uses 'disturbing the peace' rather than 'disorderly conduct.' Covers loud noise, fighting, inciting others, and public intoxication that disturbs others.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (without force); Felony (with force or violence under § 14:108.2)
penalty_max: 6 months (without force); 5 years hard labor (with force)
elements: Defendant intentionally interfered with, resisted, or obstructed a law enforcement officer
In the performance of official duties
By force or threatening force
enhancements: Use of force or violence (Felony under § 14:108.2 — Battery of a Police Officer)
notes: Simple resisting (no force) is a misdemeanor. Battery of a police officer (§ 14:34.2) is a separate felony charge. Flight from an officer (§ 14:108.1) is also separate.

penalty_max: 5 years hard labor (general); 40 years hard labor (in capital or life imprisonment case)
elements: Defendant tampered with evidence, intimidated a witness, or otherwise obstructed the administration of criminal justice
With intent to distort the outcome of any criminal investigation or proceeding
enhancements: Obstruction in a capital or life imprisonment case (up to 40 years hard labor)
notes: Louisiana's obstruction of justice statute has extremely harsh penalties when the underlying case involves capital or life imprisonment charges. General obstruction carries up to 5 years.

penalty_max: 6 months (criminal contempt); indefinite for civil contempt
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or disrupted court proceedings
Or engaged in conduct that obstructed the administration of justice
notes: Louisiana distinguishes direct contempt (in court) from constructive contempt (outside court). Direct contempt may be punished summarily. Constructive contempt requires a rule to show cause.

elements: Defendant appeared in an intoxicated condition in a public place
Such that the defendant disturbed the peace or endangered the safety of self or others
notes: Louisiana does not have a standalone public intoxication statute — it falls under disturbing the peace. Must be disruptive; mere intoxication in public is not enough.

elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal surety
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
notes: Louisiana calls this 'jumping bail.' Felony jumping bail carries up to 5 years at hard labor. Bond forfeiture and bench warrant automatically issued.

statute_title: Filing or Maintaining a False Report
offense_class: Misdemeanor; Felony (false report of terrorism under § 14:126.2)
elements: Defendant knowingly filed a false report with law enforcement
Concerning the commission of a crime
Knowing the report to be false
enhancements: False terrorism report (felony, up to 15 years)
notes: General false reporting is a misdemeanor. False terrorism reports carry up to 15 years. Swatting is treated very seriously.

elements: Defendant intentionally communicated information that the commission of a crime of violence was imminent or in progress
Knowing the information to be false
Or threatening to commit a crime of violence with intent to place a person in fear of bodily harm
notes: Louisiana uses 'terrorizing' for criminal threats. Felony carrying up to 15 years at hard labor. Includes bomb threats, mass violence threats, and threats targeting individuals.

elements: Defendant, while under oath or affirmation in a judicial proceeding
Made a false statement material to the issue or matter of inquiry
Knowing the statement to be false
notes: Perjury is a felony in Louisiana carrying up to 5 years at hard labor. Subornation of perjury (§ 14:124) — inducing another to commit perjury — carries the same penalty.

penalty_min: 1 year without probation, parole, or suspension
elements: Defendant gave or offered to give anything of apparent present or prospective value to a public official
With intent to influence the official's conduct in relation to official capacity
mandatory_minimum: 1 year without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension
notes: Public bribery carries a 1-year mandatory minimum in Louisiana. Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Louisiana has a history of aggressive public corruption prosecution.

offense_class: Felony (from felony custody); Misdemeanor (from misdemeanor custody)
penalty_max: 5 years hard labor (simple escape); 10 years hard labor (aggravated escape with violence under § 14:110(B))
elements: Defendant escaped from lawful custody
While confined pursuant to arrest or court order
enhancements: Use of violence or threat of violence (Aggravated Escape — up to 10 years)
notes: Simple escape carries up to 5 years. Aggravated escape (with force) carries up to 10 years. Includes walking away from work release.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (simple, first); Felony (aggravated under § 14:102.1 or second+)
penalty_max: 6 months (simple, first); 3 years hard labor (aggravated); 10 years hard labor (aggravated, second+)
elements: Defendant intentionally or negligently mistreated an animal
Causing unjustifiable suffering or pain
Aggravated: torture or mutilation, or causing death
enhancements: Aggravated (torture, serious injury, death) — felony up to 3 years
Second or subsequent aggravated — up to 10 years
notes: Louisiana has strengthened animal cruelty laws. Aggravated cruelty (§ 14:102.1) covering torture and mutilation is a felony. Dogfighting (§ 14:102.5) carries up to 10 years.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation proven by preponderance of the evidence
notes: Louisiana courts may revoke, modify, or continue probation. 2017 Justice Reinvestment Act introduced graduated sanctions and capped technical violation revocations. New criminal conduct typically leads to full revocation.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole determines consequences
penalty_max: Return to incarceration for remainder of sentence
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole conducts revocation hearings. 2017 reforms introduced graduated sanctions for technical violations. New criminal conduct typically results in full revocation.

penalty_min: Same as the underlying offense
elements: Defendant aided and abetted in the commission of a crime
Or procured, counseled, or commanded another to commit a crime
mandatory_minimum: Same as the underlying offense
notes: All persons concerned in the commission of a crime, whether present or absent, and whether they directly commit the act or aid and abet in its commission, are principals. Each is equally liable.

offense_class: Generally one-half the maximum sentence of the completed offense; special rules for certain crimes
penalty_max: One-half the maximum for the completed offense (e.g., attempted second-degree murder = 10-50 years)
elements: Defendant had specific intent to commit a crime
And did or omitted an act for the purpose of and tending directly toward the accomplishment thereof
notes: General rule: attempt carries one-half the maximum of the completed offense. Exceptions exist — attempted first-degree murder carries 10-50 years. Attempted armed robbery carries 10-49.5 years. Renunciation is not recognized as a defense.

offense_class: Generally one-half the maximum sentence of the target offense
penalty_max: One-half the maximum for the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed or combined with one or more persons for the specific purpose of committing any crime
And one or more parties performed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy carries one-half the maximum of the target offense. Requires an agreement and an overt act. Each conspirator is liable. Drug conspiracy has specific enhanced provisions.
